chose: While home's deploy record (state.json) can't be read, the run totals (home_deploy_runs{outcome}, home_deploy_pulls, home_deploy_pulled_bytes) are held as last read, in the gauge sweep's memory. DeployFailed keeps main's increase() rule, so it sees the reset when the deploy that heals the record rolls back, however long the gap. After a restart nothing was read, so the totals are absent until a tick reads them. The last run's time and exit code and the newest epoch, which state a current value, are NaN, as is the marker's age when the marker itself can't be read. Unreadable is still told: home-deploy/read_state is held open (invariant 9), and HomeFailuresOpen fires after about two hours. The bound: if file_host restarts while the record is unreadable and the healing deploy rolls back more than an hour after that restart, DeployFailed doesn't see it. HomeFailuresOpen has told the owner of the record only if it stayed unreadable for 2 hours, so a record unreadable for between about 1 and 2 hours across a restart, with a rollback more than an hour after that restart, is told by neither alert. The coordinator chose this on CONS-NEXT's raise, after three review rounds on server#1208's branch kept finding faults in NaN on the totals.
options: NaN on the totals, and DeployFailed bridges the gap with increase(last_over_time((x == x)[7d:5m])[1h:1m]): a gap on the graph, a nested subquery each evaluation, and a record unreadable more than 7 days before the healing deploy still hides its rollback

gray: On server#1208 the owner chose option (a), whose text says the runs gauges are 'left absent rather than 0', and said that an unreadable record is reported as a failure. This call holds those same runs gauges at their last read value instead (absent only after a restart), so it departs from that option's letter. On server#1207 the owner chose that a failed reading empties a gauge rather than freezing it; this call reads that as covering gauges that state a current level (renders, drive, last pass), not running totals, where the last value read stays true as a lower bound. The owner may read either otherwise.
undo: Put NaN back on the totals (record_state sets f64::NAN when the record is an error, and Last.totals goes), use the first option's rule for DeployFailed, and rewrite home.test.yml's C1511 case to feed NaN through a gap of two hours or more.
